epics.title: Delegation boundary
epics.objective: Make the Claude to Codex handoff briefed, bounded and measured, so a run cannot stall silently, finish half the job, or ignore rules already written down

tasks.title: stage done becomes a measurement
tasks.objective: Closing a stage stops being an assertion and becomes a measurement. The stage records where it started, and closing it compares what actually changed against what the task declared, so a run that did part of the job or none of it cannot sign itself off.
acceptance_criteria: stage start records the base commit on the stage
stage done refuses when nothing changed since the base commit, in the working tree or in commits
stage done refuses a changed product path not covered by the task's write_scope and names the offending paths; .factory/ and plans/ are exempt because the workflow itself writes them
stage done refuses when a required_tests entry cannot be resolved in the repo
stage done runs every verify_commands entry and refuses on a non-zero exit, printing the failing command
stage start --parallel refuses when the two stages' write_scope lists overlap
stage done --incomplete "<what is missing>" leaves the stage active and records the gap in the events ledger
tasks.reviewer_focus: the exemption list must not swallow the check (this repo's own product code lives under factory/, so a broad EVIDENCE_PATHS exemption would make write_scope vacuous); refusals must name what failed; verify_commands run with the repo as cwd

tasks.title: verify_commands must be runnable, not prose
tasks.objective: A per-task verify step is only a gate if it can execute. New decompositions are refused when a verify_commands entry reads as prose rather than a command, and doctor reports any active decomposition still carrying prose so it is fixed before the next stage close.
acceptance_criteria: recording a decomposition whose verify_commands entry is prose (no resolvable executable) is refused, naming the task and the entry
shipped history is untouched: the refusal applies at record time only
forge doctor reports an active decomposition carrying prose verify_commands
tasks.reviewer_focus: the runnable check must not reject legitimate shell (pipes, env prefixes, quoted args) while still catching a sentence

tasks.title: forge delegate composes the brief and the invocation
tasks.objective: Delegation becomes a command instead of a judgement. It builds a brief from artifacts that already exist, derives write permission from stage state rather than a per-request opinion, prints the exact invocation, and records the delegation with the brief's digest.
acceptance_criteria: forge delegate <task-id> writes .factory/briefs/<task-id>.md carrying the objective, acceptance criteria, write_scope with the modules already in it, required_tests, reviewer_focus, the implementer prompt, the active decisions and the matching lessons
for user-facing work the brief inlines the design rules, because the executing runtime cannot load them
write permission is derived: an active stage with a non-empty write_scope is a write run, and --read-only is the explicit exception
the printed invocation carries --prompt-file, the pinned model and effort, and the derived write flag
the delegation is recorded in .factory/delegations.jsonl against factory/schemas/delegation.json with the brief's sha256
tasks.reviewer_focus: the task id must be resolved against the recorded decomposition and never used to build a filesystem path; the ledger is append-only and union-merged

tasks.title: the brief becomes non-skippable
tasks.objective: A write-capable delegation with no brief is the failure that produces uninformed work, so the pre-tool hook denies it. The refusal names the command that fixes it, and editing the brief on disk invalidates the record.
acceptance_criteria: a --write companion call with no recorded brief for the active stage is denied, and the denial names ./forge delegate <task-id>
the same call is allowed once forge delegate has recorded the brief
editing the brief on disk after recording invalidates it and the call is denied again
the check is not skipped in plan mode
tasks.reviewer_focus: the hook must fail closed but must not deny read-only exploration; parsing of the companion command line must not be defeated by flag ordering or quoting

tasks.title: a stalled run and a missing skill become visible
tasks.objective: Two diagnostics: forge codex status reads the plugin's job registry and reports each job's status, phase, write flag and age, flagging the silent-stall signature; and doctor checks that every skill the harness demands is loadable by each runtime expected to attest it.
acceptance_criteria: forge codex status reports status, phase, write flag, age and log path per job
it flags a long-running job with no phase change, and a write:false job launched while a stage was active
it degrades to a clear unknown when the plugin path is absent, and can never fail a gate
forge doctor reports a required or advised skill that a runtime expected to attest it cannot load
forge doctor --fix installs the missing skill for that runtime
tasks.reviewer_focus: advisory means advisory: no exit code from codex status may propagate into a gate; the job registry is third-party data and must be parsed defensively

tasks.title: the delegation step is named where people look
tasks.objective: The harness gets skipped partly because the delegation step was never printed anywhere. forge next names it, the forge skill maps the intents to it, and the decision record states why these are gates rather than instructions.
acceptance_criteria: forge next names the delegation step (brief, delegate, watch, verify) when a stage is active
the forge skill maps "delegate this task" and "is Codex stuck?" to the new commands
AGENTS.md states the delegation gate in one line and stays under its 110-line cap
tasks.reviewer_focus: the AGENTS.md line count gate must actually be run, not assumed; no policy block may land in AGENTS.md
